```{r}
set.seed(100)
```

## CI for Population Proportion

::: {.callout title="Theorem 22.1"}
Let $\boldsymbol{X} = (X_1, X_2, \dots X_n)$ be independent Bernoulli random variables with success parameter $p$ and let $\boldsymbol{x} = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)$ be observed values for these. If $n$ is sufficiently large, then an approximate $100 \times (1-\alpha)\%$ confidence interval for $p$ is:

$$
\left(\hat{p} - z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n}}, \hat{p} + z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n}}\right)
$$

Where $\hat{p} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n x_i$. This result uses the fact that

$$
\hat{p} \overset{\cdot}{\sim} N\left(p, \sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)}{n}} \right)
$$

due to the CLT and the fact that $\hat{p}$ converges to $p$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$.
:::

## Ex: Exam (1)

::: {.callout title="Example 22.1"}
You administer an exam with 40 questions to a student and record whether they got each question right or wrong. You would like to construct a 95% confidence interval for $p$, the true probability of responding correctly to a question. You find that the student got 34 of the questions correct.

What is the quantile $z_{1-\alpha/2}$ and the standard error used to construct this confidence interval?
:::

. . .

```{r, echo = TRUE}
n <- 40
p_hat <- 34/n
alpha <- 0.05
z_quant <- qnorm(1-alpha/2)
std_error <- sqrt(p_hat*(1-p_hat)/n)

z_quant
std_error
```

## Ex: Survey (1)

::: {.callout title="Example 22.2"}
A survey is conducted to estimate the proportion of customers who are satisfied with a new product. Out of 120 respondents, 82 report being satisfied. You wish to construct a 90% confidence interval for $p$, the true proportion of satisfied customers.

What is the quantile $z_{1-\alpha/2}$ and the standard error used to construct this confidence interval?
:::

. . .

```{r, echo = TRUE}
n <- 120  
p_hat <- 82/n  
alpha <- 0.1 
z_quant <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)  
std_error <- sqrt(p_hat * (1 - p_hat) / n)  

z_quant  
std_error
```

## Ex: Light Bulbs (1)

::: {.callout title="Example 22.3"}
A manufacturer inspects a random sample of 75 light bulbs from a production line and finds that 15 are defective. You want to construct a 99% confidence interval for $p$, the true proportion of defective bulbs.

What is the quantile $z_{1-\alpha/2}$ and the standard error used to construct this confidence interval?
:::

. . .

```{r, echo = TRUE}
n <- 75  
p_hat <- 15/n  
alpha <- 0.01
z_quant <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)  
std_error <- sqrt(p_hat * (1 - p_hat) / n)  

z_quant  
std_error  
```

## Ex: Exam (2)

::: {.callout title="Example 22.4"}
You administer an exam with 40 questions to a student and record whether they got each question right or wrong. You find that the student got 34 of the questions correct. You would like to construct a 95% confidence interval for $p$, the true probability of responding correctly to a question.
:::

. . .

```{r, echo = TRUE}
n <- 40
p_hat <- 34/n
alpha <- 0.05
z_quant <- qnorm(1-alpha/2)
std_error <- sqrt(p_hat*(1-p_hat)/n)

p_hat + c(-1, 1)*z_quant*std_error
```

## Ex: Survey (2)

::: {.callout title="Example 22.5"}
A survey is conducted to estimate the proportion of customers who are satisfied with a new product. Out of 120 respondents, 82 report being satisfied. You wish to construct a 90% confidence interval for $p$, the true proportion of satisfied customers.
:::

. . .

```{r, echo = TRUE}
n <- 120  
p_hat <- 82/n  
alpha <- 0.1 
z_quant <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)  
std_error <- sqrt(p_hat * (1 - p_hat) / n)  

p_hat + c(-1, 1)*z_quant*std_error
```

## Ex: Light Bulbs (2)

::: {.callout title="Example 22.6"}
A manufacturer inspects a random sample of 75 light bulbs from a production line and finds that 15 are defective. You want to construct a 99% confidence interval for $p$, the true proportion of defective bulbs.
:::

. . .

```{r, echo = TRUE}
n <- 75  
p_hat <- 15/n  
alpha <- 0.01
z_quant <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)  
std_error <- sqrt(p_hat * (1 - p_hat) / n)  

p_hat + c(-1, 1)*z_quant*std_error
```
